What capabilities do your AI agents contain? Our AI agent solutions cover a wide range of capabilities – including task automation, data analysis, data extraction, code generation, and content creation. Whether you need AI agents or enterprise AI solutions, we build them to your exact specifications. What is the estimated cost to develop an AI agent? The cost to develop an AI agent depends on its features and integration requirements. What is an AI agent and how does it work? An AI agent is software that perceives its environment, makes decisions, and takes actions autonomously to complete a goal – without needing step-by-step human instructions. Think of it as a digital worker that can browse, analyze, write, call APIs, and coordinate with other agents. Unlike a basic chatbot that just responds, an AI agent plans, executes tasks, and adapts when things don’t go as expected. How can AI agents actually help my business? AI agents handle repetitive, time-consuming work – customer support triage, data extraction, report generation, lead qualification, internal ticket routing. They work around the clock without fatigue and scale instantly. For businesses, the impact shows up in faster turnaround times, lower operational costs, and staff freed up for higher-value work. The use case varies by industry, but the underlying benefit is the same: less manual effort, more consistent output. Which industries can benefit from AI agent development? Most industries have strong use cases – finance (fraud detection, compliance monitoring), healthcare (patient intake, clinical documentation), e-commerce (personalized recommendations, order tracking), HR (resume screening, onboarding workflows), and logistics (route optimization, shipment tracking). At Yudiz, we’ve worked across multiple sectors and can map the right agent architecture to your specific business process. If your team does repetitive, rule-based, or data-heavy work – AI agents are worth exploring. Do I need a technical team to implement AI agents in my business? No. You don’t need in-house AI engineers to get started. You need a clear picture of the business problem you want to solve – the technical side is what we handle. We work with operations, product, and business teams directly to understand workflows and translate them into working agent solutions. The simpler your problem statement, the faster the build. What AI frameworks and tools does Yudiz use to build AI agents? We use production-ready frameworks depending on the agent’s complexity and use case. This includes LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen for multi-agent orchestration, combined with LLMs like GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini for reasoning. For memory and retrieval, we use vector databases like Pinecone or Weaviate. The framework choice is driven by your use case, not what’s trending. What are the most common use cases for AI agents? The most common ones we see: automated customer support agents that resolve queries without human intervention, research agents that gather and summarize information on demand, sales agents that qualify leads and draft outreach, data pipeline agents that extract and process structured data, and internal ops agents that route requests, generate reports, or manage approvals. Most businesses start with one high-impact use case and expand from there. How do AI agents help with faster and better decision-making? AI agents process large amounts of data in real time – customer signals, market data, operational metrics – and surface the relevant information exactly when a decision needs to be made. Instead of a manager waiting for a weekly report, an agent can flag anomalies, summarize trends, or trigger an action the moment a threshold is crossed. Decisions get faster because the information gap shrinks. Can AI agents scale as my business grows? Yes, a single agent architecture that handles 100 requests today can handle 10,000 tomorrow with infrastructure scaling, not headcount scaling. Multi-agent systems can also be extended – add a new agent for a new workflow without rebuilding what’s already running. The marginal cost of scaling an AI agent is far lower than scaling a human team. What is AgentOps and do you support it? AgentOps is the practice of monitoring, evaluating, and maintaining AI agents once they’re live – similar to DevOps for software. It covers tracking agent performance, catching failures, logging decisions, and updating agents as underlying models or business rules change. Without it, agents drift, make unexpected errors, or become outdated silently. Building an agent is step one; keeping it reliable is the ongoing work. You cannot copy content of this page

Prompt Research Keyword research tells you what people type into Google. Prompt research tells you what they ask AI tools. These are often longer, more specific questions, like "best SEO agency for a dentist in London" or "which AI tool should I use for Shorts editing". A good provider maps the prompts your buyers ask, checks who gets named in the answers today, and finds the gaps where nobody strong is being cited yet. That's your target list. Ask: how do you choose which prompts to go after? Want to see your own prompt gaps? Get a free SEO strategy session and we'll show you which AI answers name your competitors instead of you. 2. AI Visibility Tracking If nobody tracks it, nobody knows if it's working. AI visibility tracking means checking, on a schedule, whether your brand shows up in AI answers for your target prompts, and which pages get cited as sources. Rankings still matter, but they're only half the picture now. One of my sites, for example, got over 9,600 impressions in Google's AI features in a single day. You want to see numbers like that in your reports. Ask: what will my monthly report show about AI answers, not just rankings? 3. Answer-Ready Content AI tools pull short, clear answers. So your pages need to answer the question in the first sentence, then back it up. That means direct openings, clean headings, plain-English FAQs and tables that compare options simply. This isn't about stuffing keywords. It's about making your page the easiest one to quote. Ask: show me a page you wrote that gets quoted in an AI answer. 4. Case-Study Content This is the service most providers skip, and it's the one that matters most. AI can summarise generic advice from anywhere. What it can't make up is your first-hand data: tests, results, screenshots and what didn't work. It's the first move in my Answer Engine framework, be the source. When I search "best GEO expert" in Google, the AI answer names me first and says I'm known for documenting GEO experiments and public testing. That came from publishing real tests, not opinions. Ask: how will you turn our results into content AI will cite? 📺 Watch: Hermes AI + Kaparthy LLM Wiki is INSANE! 5. Entity and Schema Work AI tools need to understand who you are, what you do and how you connect to your topic. Entity work makes that clear and consistent across your site, your profiles and the wider web. Schema markup, like Organization, Article and FAQPage, helps machines read your pages correctly. One warning here. Google's updated guidance on 1 October 2026 says to fact-check and review all AI-assisted content before publishing, and that includes structured data, metadata and image alt text. Sloppy auto-generated schema is a risk. Ask: who checks the schema before it goes live? 6. Multi-Site and Platform Presence This is move two of the Answer Engine: be everywhere. If the AI sees the same name across several top results, from different sites and platforms, each with its own angle, it's far more likely to recommend that name. That's how the AI answer for "best Hermes AI SEO expert" ends up recommending me. It's sourced from my own content on several platforms. It also protects you: if one site drops, the others stay. Communities, subreddits like r/AISEOInsider, YouTube and partner sites all count. Ask: beyond my website, where will my brand show up? 7. Link Building on Cited Sources AI answers lean on pages that already rank and sites that are trusted. So the smartest link building targets the exact sources AI tools already cite for your topic. Get mentioned there, and you get pulled into the answer. Do it the clean way: manual outreach, real sites, no PBNs, no link farms. For "best HARO agency", the AI Overview lists five suppliers, and Goldie Agency is the one it links out to first. Links did a lot of that work. Ask: where exactly do your links come from? 8. Trend-First Publishing Move three of the Answer Engine: be first. When a new tool, model or update drops, the first good page often becomes the source AI tools quote. I aim to publish on trending topics within about 24 hours, before anyone else has a page. It works. My "best AI SEO community" article was ranking three days after it was published, with the AI Profit Boardroom at number one and my free community at number two, and the AI Overview citing them more than once. Explore FinOps Services FAQ LLM cost optimization: frequently asked questions What is LLM cost optimization? LLM cost optimization is the practice of reducing the cost of running large language model workloads — through model routing, prompt/response caching, token and context efficiency, and inference cost management — while keeping output quality where it needs to be. What is model routing and how does it reduce LLM costs? Model routing sends each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it well — a simple classification task doesn't need your most expensive frontier model — instead of routing every request to a single, general-purpose (and usually most expensive) model by default. How does caching reduce LLM inference costs? Prompt and response caching avoids paying for the same or highly similar LLM call twice — common for repeated queries, shared system prompts, or retrieval results that don't change often — and can meaningfully cut token spend at scale. How do you manage token and context window costs? We tune prompt design and context-window usage — trimming unnecessary context, summarizing long histories, and right-sizing retrieved context in RAG pipelines — since token count drives cost directly on most LLM pricing models. How does LLM cost optimization fit into a broader AI FinOps practice? LLM cost optimization is the token- and inference-level layer of AI FinOps, working alongside GenAI FinOps (platform and model-selection economics), AI Cost Optimization (GPU/infrastructure rightsizing) and AI Cost Management (visibility and governance).
